sub_answers.sub_question: Which targeted export-promotion campaigns, export hubs, incubation programs, or sector-specific initiatives has the agency implemented to help film producers, fashion designers, and music creators reach international markets? sub_answers.text: The Trinidad and Tobago Creative Industries Company Limited (CreativeTT) was established in 2015 as a state agency to stimulate and facilitate the business development and export activities of the Creative Industries in Trinidad and Tobago [d3565457s47p0]. CreativeTT is responsible for the strategic and business development of three niche areas under its purview: Music, Film and Fashion [d3565457s47p0]. The subsidiaries MusicTT, FilmTT and FashionTT were established to fulfil CreativeTT’s mandate to support those sectors’ business development and export activities [d3565457s47p0].

Which international industry events, trade missions, buyer-seller forums, co-marketing partnerships, or government-to-government market-access agreements does the agency organize, sponsor, or maintain relationships with to promote film, fashion, and music exports? What concrete capacity-building offerings does the agency deliver to creatives for export readiness — for example export training courses, one-on-one export coaching, mentorship networks, market-entry strategy workshops, IP/legal clinics, or digital commerce upskilling — and what are the curricula, frequency, target participants, and measures of outcomes?

Which audit reports, parliamentary inquiries, ombudsman investigations, comptroller or auditor-general findings have flagged governance weaknesses, budgetary irregularities, non-compliance with financial controls, or failures of accountability at the agency, and what were the specific findings, recommendations and dates of those reports?
sub_answers.text: The Kerala High Court examined audited accounts of the Travancore Devaswom Board's Global Ayyappa Sangamam and found several irregularities, including discrepancies between public claims and audit figures and improper accounting of items distributed to devotees [d15307854s10p0]. An ECFA audit of the Christian Research Institute in 2003 found CRI out of compliance with a number of financial standards and resulted in sanctions requiring board strengthening and a significant reimbursement [d2433368s6p0]. The Commission on Audit ordered the disallowance of a P10-million transaction related to Joel Villanueva, and the Ombudsman ordered his dismissal for grave misconduct and serious dishonesty over alleged misuse of funds and fabricated supporting documents (decision dated November 14, 2016) [d49639697s5p0]. Media reports and internal memoranda by Pius Bigirimana flagged financial irregularities in the Office of the Prime Minister’s accounting systems and these memoranda were examined during investigations into the OPM funds scandal [d82370597s10p0]. Annual audit reports are submitted publicly to Parliament by the Auditor General (consolidated reports available for FY 2023–24 and FY 2022–23), indicating a regular public reporting mechanism for audit findings [d81396933s3p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What formal criticisms have business groups, chambers of commerce, export councils, startup accelerators, creative industry trade associations or major exporters published about the agency’s performance—for example complaints about funding levels, application backlogs, lack of measurable outcomes, regional coverage gaps or duplication of services—and which organizations made those critiques and when?

Are there documented instances—media investigations, watchdog reports, court filings or internal disclosures—alleging conflicts of interest, biased contract awards, tender irregularities, appointments of relatives or cronies, undisclosed financial ties, or related-party transactions involving the agency’s executives or board members, and what evidence or official findings support those allegations?
sub_answers.text: CRI's 1992 withdrawal from ECFA was alleged by critics to have been to avoid restrictions on financial dealings with its chief executive, and a 2003 ECFA audit found CRI out of compliance with financial standards leading to sanctions and requirements to strengthen the board, which suggests documented concerns about conflicted financial relationships involving leadership [d2433368s6p0]. The Ombudsman's finding against Joel Villanueva described funds being released through bogus NGOs, fabricated beneficiary lists, and forged supporting documents, which are documented allegations of corrupt awarding and misuse of funds by a public official [d49639697s5p0].
